title: Crown, wisdom, understanding
hook: Keter, Chochmah, Binah: will, the flash of an idea, and its unfolding

segments.voice: Yesterday, the sefirot: ten lights, from crown down to kingship, one fire with many tongues of flame. Your line was ten lights. Which name caught on something in your day? Day one thousand one hundred seventy-six.

In the shower, on a walk, halfway through washing a pan: the idea arrives. All at once, whole, before you have words for it. The shape of the answer is there, but it can't be explained yet. Then comes the long part. You sit down, and you work it out, step by step, piece by piece, until the flash becomes a plan someone else could follow. And underneath both, before either, there was something quieter: the wanting to solve it in the first place. Kabbalists saw those three moments at the very top of the ten lights. Today we start at the top, with the crown.
screen: `THE IDEA ARRIVES, WHOLE.` → `THEN THE LONG WORKING OUT.` → `BEFORE BOTH, YOU WANTED IT.`

segments.voice: Keter, Chochmah, Binah. Crown, wisdom, understanding. Turn them four ways. First, the crown. A crown sits above the head, not inside it. Kabbalists place Keter above thought, and link it to will: the deep wanting that comes before any idea. Some teachers say so little can be said of it that it borders on Ein Sof itself. Second, wisdom, Chochmah. The flash. The point of light before it has length or width. The book of Job asks, "But where shall wisdom be found?" In Hebrew the word for where can also be read as from nothing, and kabbalists heard Job saying that wisdom comes from nothing: out of the hidden crown, a sudden point. Third, understanding, Binah. The unfolding. Binah takes the point and gives it room, rooms and corridors and details, the way a seed becomes a plant. Kabbalists picture the two as a pair, a father and a mother. The flash needs the unfolding, or it stays a spark. The unfolding needs the flash, or it has nothing to build. Fourth, where the three words meet. You met Bezalel a few days ago, joining letters. When the Torah first introduces him, the craftsman of the tabernacle, God fills him "with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge." Wisdom, understanding, knowledge: in Hebrew chochmah, binah, da'at, the three words one Hasidic school, Chabad, took as its name. And look back across this week: reason serving faith, the received tradition, the careful doorway, the letters, the One without end, the ten lights, and now the top three. A week spent climbing to the crown.
screen: `CROWN: THE WILL ABOVE THOUGHT.` · `WISDOM: THE FLASH FROM NOTHING.` · `UNDERSTANDING: THE UNFOLDING.` · `WISDOM, UNDERSTANDING, KNOWLEDGE.` · then, large: `THE FLASH AND THE UNFOLDING.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice one idea arriving. Settle, and breathe, and let your mind go quiet without forcing it. Hold one small question in front of you, something real: what to cook tonight, what to say to someone, how to begin a task. Don't chase the answer. Just wait, the way you'd wait for a bird to land. When something arrives, notice the moment before it had words. Then let it unfold, slowly, into one plain sentence. Flash, then unfolding. If nothing comes, notice the wanting underneath, and rest there. The bell holds the time.
Crown. Keter, the top of the ten lights: the will that sits above thought, before wisdom flashes and understanding unfolds. Today's word.
Your line: the flash and the unfolding. Today, when an idea comes to you, give it a few quiet minutes to unfold before you act on it. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-six.

howItsDone: In Kabbalah, Keter, Chochmah and Binah are taught as the highest sefirot; Chabad Hasidism takes its name from Chochmah, Binah and Da'at, and its teaching applies them to how a person thinks.

what a scholar hears: Job 28:12 read as wisdom coming from nothing, and Exodus 31:3's wisdom, understanding and knowledge, the root of the Hasidic name Chabad.

Keter linked to will, Chochmah as the flash/point, Binah as unfolding, and the father/mother pairing are general kabbalistic teaching, paraphrased; the Zohar source line is generic. Please supply a more exact reference or accept.
